evals.prompt: We're building a parking lot management system. I want to figure out the domain concepts before we write any code or design any API. Write use-cases for the main flows — entering, exiting, and paying — then extract the domain concepts.
evals.expected_output: Use-cases in stripped-down Cockburn format (Use Case / Actor / Goal / Main flow) for the key parking lot flows, followed by concept documents for each extracted concept with OKF frontmatter.
expectations: At least two use-cases are produced, each with Use Case, Actor, Goal, and Main flow fields
Actors are named domain roles — not generic labels like 'User' or 'Person'
Main flow steps use domain language — no HTTP verbs, endpoint paths, or CRUD verbs (Create/Read/Update/Delete)
At least one domain object with lifecycle states is extracted — e.g. a parking space or session with states like available/occupied
ParkingSpace (or equivalent) and a session/ticket concept are extracted as separate domain objects — they have different lifecycles
Concept documents include OKF frontmatter with type: concept, title, description, and tags fields
Concept tags use the defined kind vocabulary: entity, value-object, domain-event, actor, or action
No concept is named after a CRUD operation or wire shape (e.g. CreateSpaceRequest, UpdateTicketResponse)

evals.prompt: I need to gather requirements for a library management system. Start with what happens when a member borrows a book and work outward from there. I want domain use-cases and concept documents — no API design yet.
evals.expected_output: Use-cases covering the borrowing lifecycle and any related flows, followed by concept documents. The Book/Copy distinction should emerge.
expectations: At least two use-cases are produced, each with Use Case, Actor, Goal, and Main flow fields
Actors include Member and Librarian (or equivalent named roles)
Main flow steps use domain language — no HTTP verbs, endpoint paths, or CRUD verbs
Both Book (title) and Copy (physical item) are extracted as separate domain objects, or the skill asks a clarifying question that surfaces the distinction
Loan is extracted as a domain object with lifecycle states — e.g. active, overdue, returned
Concept documents include OKF frontmatter with type: concept, title, description, and tags fields
Concept tags use the defined kind vocabulary: entity, value-object, domain-event, actor, or action
No concept is named after a database table or CRUD operation

evals.prompt: We're designing a hotel booking system. Before we touch any schema or API, I want to map out the domain. Write use-cases covering the guest experience and the front desk side, then extract the domain concepts.
evals.expected_output: Use-cases for the guest and front desk flows, followed by concept documents. The Reservation/Stay distinction should emerge.
expectations: At least three use-cases are produced, each with Use Case, Actor, Goal, and Main flow fields
Actors include Guest and a front desk role (Receptionist, FrontDesk, or equivalent named role)
Main flow steps use domain language — no HTTP verbs, endpoint paths, or CRUD verbs
Reservation and Stay (or equivalent) are extracted as separate domain objects with different lifecycles — a future commitment vs. an active occupancy
Room is extracted as a domain object with availability lifecycle states
Concept documents include OKF frontmatter with type: concept, title, description, and tags fields
Concept tags use the defined kind vocabulary: entity, value-object, domain-event, actor, or action
No concept is named after a wire shape, endpoint, or database table

evals.prompt: We're building a ride-sharing app similar to Uber. Write domain use-cases for the core flows — requesting a ride, accepting a trip offer, and completing a trip — then extract the domain concepts.
evals.expected_output: Use-cases for the rider and driver flows, followed by concept documents including Trip with its full lifecycle.
expectations: At least three use-cases are produced, each with Use Case, Actor, Goal, and Main flow fields
Actors include Rider and Driver as distinct named roles
Main flow steps use domain language — no HTTP verbs, endpoint paths, or CRUD verbs
Trip is extracted as a domain object with multiple lifecycle states (at minimum: requested, accepted, in progress, completed)
Driver availability is recognised as distinct from driver account status — either as a separate concept or as an explicit note in a use-case step
Concept documents include OKF frontmatter with type: concept, title, description, and tags fields
Concept tags use the defined kind vocabulary: entity, value-object, domain-event, actor, or action
No concept is named after a CRUD operation, wire shape, or endpoint
